Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has announced plans to build a second international African village in Umuahia, following the one in Kigali, Rwanda. Otti made the disclosure on Saturday during the 2026 Abia Day Celebration held at the Indoor Sports Hall of the Moshood Abiola Stadium, Abuja. The event was organised by the Abia Development Organisation, Abuja Branch, with the theme, “Abia Ekulie La” (Abia has risen). Following a request by the group, Otti said, “I like the request about a village or Diaspora City. I want to assure you that we have started working on the Diaspora City since last year. So, we are on it, and by the time we are done, you will be called upon to take advantage of it. “We are also working on another city in liaison with international organisations. Just like what you have in Kigali – the only international village in Africa. The second one will be in Umuahia, Abia State of Nigeria”. The Governor congratulated them for their continued support for their people at home through remittances, which he said contribute significantly to the economic development of the state, and urged them to consider bringing part of their businesses back home. And rational investors will now come from the supply side. So, this is the time for you to begin to think home”, and thanked them for endorsing him for a second term. “For us, the most important job of government is to make people happy, and to see to their welfare and security. And I can assure you that the government you have, the government you put in place through the glory of God in 2023, will never fail you,” the Governor further assured. In his keynote address titled, “Abia Ekulie La” (Abia has Risen): The Role of Good Governance, Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe, who represents Abia South Senatorial District, stated emphatically that Abia State was beginning to reverse decades of developmental setbacks under Governor Otti’s visionary and intentional leadership. In his opening remarks, the Chairman of the occasion and Founder of the Unubiko Foundation, Chief James Ume, described the Abia Day celebration in Abuja as an opportunity for Abians to come together, celebrate, engage in honest conversations and honour individuals who have contributed to the advancement of the state.
